response.sql: SELECT SUM(state_total) AS total_of_state_totals, AVG(invoice_count) AS avg_invoices_per_state FROM (SELECT c.State AS state, SUM(i.Total) AS state_total, COUNT(i.InvoiceId) AS invoice_count FROM Invoice i JOIN Customer c ON c.CustomerId = i.CustomerId WHERE i.InvoiceDate BETWEEN '2010-06-22 00:00:00' AND '2012-06-26 00:00:00' GROUP BY c.State) AS state_groups;

assumptions.assumption: InvoiceDate is stored as 'YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS' text, so the BETWEEN text comparison includes the full day of 2012-06-26 only at exactly 00:00:00 and excludes later times that day, as the request's text comparison specifies.
Grouping is by Customer.State, so each state is one group; customers with a NULL State form a single group together, which GROUP BY does by default.
Empty-string or whitespace-only State values are not treated as missing; only NULL is grouped as the no-state group.
'Average number of invoices per state' is the mean of the per-state invoice counts, with the NULL-state group counted as one state; no ROUND is applied, so the AVG result is unrounded.
